modalLead: Fresh, made to work. It shipped depending on a setting most installs have switched off — link previews — so it could never find a feed and sat there saying nothing was new. It looks for its own feeds now, says what it found, and can tell you which of your bookmarks take part at all. Plus the modifier click every browser honours, given back.

items.text: Fresh introduces itself. A card in the corner offers it once, with a short walkthrough: what the count on a row means, the collection it gathers into, why it costs almost nothing, and what it is not — no articles, no reading list. The last step turns it on if you want it. It is also explained in full under Config → Help → Monitoring.

Fresh finds its own feeds. It used to learn where a feed lived only when a link preview happened to be fetched — so with previews switched off it could never find anything, and sat there saying nothing was new. Switching it on now checks your saved pages itself, and the setting says what it found: how many were asked, and how many publish a feed at all.
Fresh has its own tab under Behavior, between Inbox and Status & health — it used to be the fourth panel down a tab about link checking, which asks a different question.

See which bookmarks can tell you anything. The bookmark editor names the feed behind a link when there is one, status:feed finds them all in one search, and — if you want it — a switch on the Fresh tab marks those rows even when nothing is new. That last one is off by default: a mark on twenty quiet rows is the noise Fresh is meant to spare you.

What this says. Statistics opens with the three things its figures actually mean — where your opening lands, what is going unread, what is not answering — each with the button that acts on it. Nothing to report means nothing shown.
The tiles say which way a count moved. nextDash has been recording a point a day all along; the overview reads it now. +7 this week when it moved, and silence when it did not.
Rows hand off, tabs can be linked. A most-opened bookmark or a category now takes you to the list where you can act on it, and every tab carries a link you can copy.
The export carries every tab. Downloading from Overview used to leave the Inbox and Health figures out of a complete-looking file.

A filtered list is a link now. What you searched, the page, the category, the tag and the sort all live in the address bar — so “the 41 untagged on Work” is something you can bookmark or send to yourself, and a reload keeps it.
An empty list says why. It used to blame your search whatever was actually narrowing it.
A selection survives a filter change, so you can tick the untagged and then add the duplicates. The bar says how many of them the current filter is hiding.
Undo for bulk tags, pins and availability, in the same eight-second toast delete already had.
Sort by page, recent or most opened in one click, and ask what changed in the last week — the question that follows an import.

A long list stays quick. The list now draws the rows around what you are looking at instead of every row it has loaded — on a library of two thousand that is a thousand elements on the page instead of sixty-seven thousand, with the scrollbar unchanged and nothing jumping.

Ctrl/Cmd+click opens a bookmark in a new tab again. It used to tick the row for a bulk action instead — the one modifier every link on the web honours, doing the opposite of what it does everywhere else, and on a Mac with the row menu on top. Ticking a row with the mouse is Alt+click now.
The row menu in Health shows all of itself. It used to cap at a fixed height and scroll inside, which hid whatever was at the bottom of the list.

Help describes the config you actually have. Behavior said five sub-tabs and has seven; the grid settings were said to live on a tab that no longer exists; Data & backups described one Maintenance panel where there are now three tabs; the section list left out About. All four corrected, in every language.
Tips has its own filter, narrowing to the single tip rather than the group, and a help topic that continues on another tab now links straight to the panel it continues in.
